readiness_codes.-1: experiment not relevant for this Moon target

categories.label: Terrain & topography
categories.how: Measured relief, slope, roughness and steep-ground share, same 80 m elevation processing on both bodies (the fine-tuned DINOv2 model is evaluated but does not improve the score, so it is not used)

categories.label: Geology & surface materials
categories.how: BGE-small text encoder fine-tuned contrastively on lunar map units vs Earth lithology, plus a lithology-match term

categories.label: Temperature
categories.how: Night minimum temperature plus the light-twin sun terms. Closest approach only: no Earth site is lunar-cold, so this ranks how cold and polar the site is. Not part of the overall score

categories.label: Sunlight & illumination
categories.how: Noon sun height and grazing-sun share in the Earth light-twin month (the month whose sun is closest to the Moon target's). A real overlap for ~35-40% of Earth sites; Earth still has a 24 h day and a scattering sky. Calibrated on draft anchors

categories.label: Water, ice & permafrost
categories.how: Frozen ground within ~1 m, distance from flat bare ground to ice, absence of liquid water

categories.label: Dust & regolith
categories.how: Bare ground share and volcanic tephra, compared with the known lunar regolith (Apollo samples: bare, dry, fine). Same for every Moon target, so not part of the overall score

categories.label: Biological sterility
categories.how: How lifeless the Earth site is (vegetation greenness, rainfall), compared with the sterile Moon. Same for every Moon target, capped at 0.6, not part of the overall score

categories.label: Caves & lava tubes
categories.how: Rule: known lava-tube region / basaltic volcano / no tubes, against the Tranquillitatis pit (an LRO-imaged skylight). Only for that target

categories.label: Landing & operations
categories.how: Calibrated terrain and ice scores plus slope hazard, penalty for forest / towns / water

experiments.name: Landing hazard detection & terrain-relative navigation
also_account_for: Lander-scale hazards (boulders, small craters) are below the 500 m slope baseline; verify with metre-scale DEMs.
Plume-surface interaction in vacuum (high-speed ejecta, no drag) cannot be reproduced outdoors on Earth.
Optical and lidar hazard detection must be tested under low-sun, no-skylight lighting (night tests with artificial light).
Vegetation, buildings and DSM artefacts can create false hazards on Earth.

experiments.name: Rover mobility & navigation
also_account_for: 1/6 g lowers wheel normal load: traction and sinkage change non-linearly; add mass-scaled or offloaded tests on a geotechnical simulant (e.g. GRC-3).
Moist, vegetated or rounded-grain Earth soils differ from dry, angular, compact lunar regolith.
No GNSS on the Moon: switch GPS off and navigate visually or by terrain-relative methods.
Low sun and black shadows degrade stereo vision; ~1.3 s latency and line-of-sight loss at the pole.

experiments.name: Ice prospecting (GPR, neutron spectrometer, drill-based detection)
also_account_for: Ice at 250-273 K (Earth) vs 25-110 K (Moon) changes GPR velocity/attenuation and drill response.
Earth's atmosphere blocks the cosmic-ray neutron source used for passive lunar neutron spectroscopy; Earth field tests need an active neutron source.
Earth permafrost contains liquid films, salts and organics; lunar ice carries other volatiles (CO, CO2, NH3, H2S, CH3OH).
Lunar ice distribution is set by sublimation in vacuum, not by climate or hydrology.

experiments.name: ISRU: excavation and extraction of icy regolith
also_account_for: In vacuum ice sublimates instead of melting: heating and vapour capture must be validated in a thermal-vacuum chamber.
Ice-cemented regolith at cryogenic temperature is much harder than Earth permafrost near 0 C.
Volatile contaminants (H2S, NH3, CO2 ...) need handling.
PSR operations: no sunlight for power, extreme cold soak.

experiments.name: Regolith excavation, berms, landing pads, sintering
also_account_for: 1/6 g reduces excavator weight and reaction force; lunar regolith is very compact below ~30 cm with interlocking angular grains.
Sintering and microwave heating depend on glass and nanophase iron absent from Earth tephra.
No water for concrete; binders outgas in vacuum.

experiments.name: Thermal control & power survival (extreme cold, long shadow/night)
also_account_for: No convection in vacuum: radiative loss dominates; Earth wind chill is the wrong heat-transfer mode.
PSR 25-110 K and long cold soaks cannot be reached outdoors (Earth minimum ~180 K): qualify in cryo-TVAC.
Earth polar night is seasonal and comes with an atmosphere; lunar shadow periods are set by topography.

experiments.name: Illumination & solar-power planning, low-sun-angle vision
also_account_for: Lunar south-pole sun stays within ~1.5 deg of the horizon; use LOLA illumination maps for numbers and Earth sites for procedures only.
No atmospheric scattering on the Moon: shadows are black.
Clouds and weather cut Earth solar input; the Moon has none.

experiments.name: Habitat, human operations, crew isolation
also_account_for: Isolation/remoteness is not scored by any category: prefer sites tagged 'isolation' (e.g. Concordia, HMP, MDRS).
No Earth site forces suited EVA and airlock cycles.
Lunar surface radiation ~1.4 mSv/day; ~3-day return to Earth; ~2.6 s round-trip comms.

experiments.name: Dust mitigation (seals, coatings, filters, suits)
also_account_for: Lunar dust is charged and moved by plume ejecta and electrostatics, not wind; Earth dust is wind-driven and moist.
Sharp glassy agglutinates are more abrasive than weathered Earth dust.
Verify seals and mechanisms in dirty-vacuum chambers with simulant.

experiments.name: Instrument field tests: spectrometers / mineralogy (VNIR, Raman, LIBS, XRF)
also_account_for: No space weathering on Earth (no nanophase-iron darkening and reddening).
Terrestrial anorthosite is more sodic than lunar ferroan anorthosite.
Atmospheric water bands (VNIR) and different LIBS plasma at 1 atm; lichen/biofilm coatings on Earth rocks.

experiments.name: Instrument field tests: GPR and drilling
also_account_for: Drilling in vacuum: no air cooling or flushing of cuttings; ice cuttings sublimate.
Cryogenic ice-regolith is much harder than Earth permafrost.
Earth subsurface moisture and salts dominate GPR attenuation.

experiments.name: Planetary protection, contamination blanks, life-detection false positives
also_account_for: No Earth surface is sterile; every blank still carries microbes and organics.
Stations and camps raise local contamination.
COSPAR policy for lunar polar / PSR missions asks for an organic-materials inventory (check the current category definitions).

experiments.name: Cave / pit robotics (skylight descent, mapping, comms)
also_account_for: Lunar pits/tubes may be far larger than terrestrial tubes.
Diviner-based studies estimate the shaded Tranquillitatis pit floor stays near ~290 K (verify before quoting).
Underground: no comms or GNSS; skylight descent by tether.
Earth caves are humid, biologically active and shaped by water.

experiments.name: Astronaut field-geology & EVA training
also_account_for: Suit dexterity, EVA time limits and 1/6 g gait are not reproduced.
Low sun and black shadows at the pole change what can be seen.
Earth outcrops are weathered and often vegetated.

earth_cannot_reproduce.consequence: traction, sinkage, plume ejecta ballistics, excavation reaction forces, structural loads, human gait and EVA workload all differ
earth_cannot_reproduce.cover_with: gravity-offload rigs, mass-scaled rovers, parabolic flights, simulation

earth_cannot_reproduce.earth_best: ~60-65 kPa at the highest analog sites (e.g. Dome C at 3,233 m)
earth_cannot_reproduce.consequence: no convective cooling, ice sublimates instead of melting, outgassing, cold welding, electrostatic dust, no wind; LIBS and other instruments behave differently
earth_cannot_reproduce.cover_with: thermal-vacuum (TVAC) and dirty-vacuum chambers with regolith simulant

earth_cannot_reproduce.moon: galactic cosmic rays + solar particle events; ~1.4 mSv/day dose equivalent measured by Chang'e-4 (~200x Earth surface background)
earth_cannot_reproduce.earth_best: atmosphere and magnetosphere shield every Earth site
earth_cannot_reproduce.consequence: electronics single-event effects, materials ageing, crew dose limits

earth_cannot_reproduce.earth_best: ~180-190 K surface minimum on the East Antarctic plateau
earth_cannot_reproduce.consequence: material embrittlement, lubricant and battery failure, cryogenic ice strength, volatile trapping
earth_cannot_reproduce.cover_with: cryo-vacuum chambers, LN2 (77 K) cold plates

earth_cannot_reproduce.moon: sun within ~1.5 deg of the horizon plus topography; black shadows with no skylight
earth_cannot_reproduce.earth_best: atmospheric scattering fills shadows; sun never that low for long except near the poles
earth_cannot_reproduce.consequence: vision, navigation and solar-power results do not transfer
earth_cannot_reproduce.cover_with: night tests with low-angle artificial light; ray-traced lunar illumination (LOLA)

earth_cannot_reproduce.moon: agglutinates, glass, nanophase iron, sharp angular grains, very compact below ~30 cm
earth_cannot_reproduce.earth_best: chemically weathered, rounded, moist soils with organics
earth_cannot_reproduce.cover_with: certified simulants (e.g. LHS-1 / NU-LHT highland, LMS-1 / JSC-1A mare, GRC-3 geotechnical)

earth_cannot_reproduce.moon: UV photoemission and solar-wind plasma charge the surface
earth_cannot_reproduce.consequence: dust adhesion and levitation behave differently
contamination blanks and life-detection false positives

earth_cannot_reproduce.moon: ~1.3 s one-way light time; no direct-to-Earth line of sight behind south-pole terrain
earth_cannot_reproduce.cover_with: simulated latency and blackout windows in analog ops

dust_reference.note: fines = % finer than 50 um; lunar soil median grain size ~70 um (the brief's '70-80% sand-sized' would be fines ~25%; kept the 45% of categories.json)

limitations: No ground truth exists for analog quality: the -1..+1 scale is set by draft expert anchors (all still marked needs_review).
Temperature and sun angle never overlap between Moon and Earth: thermal scores are closest-approach (a latitude ranking), not similarity, and are left out of the overall score.

Dust/regolith and sterility compare Earth sites with known lunar constants (Apollo regolith, sterile Moon), so they rank Earth sites the same way for every Moon target and are left out of the overall score.
Earth climate layers are coarser (5-50 km) than the 10 km tiles; Antarctica lacks land-cover, soil and rainfall layers.
Lunar geology comes from a 1:5M map plus the known composition of mare vs highland crust, not per-tile mineralogy.
Thermal scores for the Tranquillitatis pit are extrapolated (thermal anchors are all polar).
Gravity, vacuum, radiation and 25-110 K shadowed temperatures cannot be reproduced on Earth and are never scored.
